raw_case_text: In February 2016, a 19-year-old woman coming from Ivory Coast was admitted to a peripheral hospital of our city for persistent fever. After she resulted positive for a screening HIV-Ab test, she was referred to the Infectious and Tropical Diseases Department. At admission she had deep asthenia, chills, fever (max 38.8 C), and tachycardia (110 bpm); examination revealed mono-lateral tonsillar hypertrophy and submandibular lymphadenopathy. Laboratory investigations showed pancytopenia (haemoglobin 8.7 g/dL - normal value 12.0-16.0 g/dL, white blood cells 3,050/muL -n.v. 4.00-10.80x103/muL, platelets 80,000/muL - n.v. 130-400x103/muL), increased lactate dehydrogenase (5,201 U/L - n.v. 136-234 U/L ), increased levels of C Reactive Protein (63.3 mg/L - n.v. < 5.0 mg/L ), and high ferritin and triglycerides serum levels (> 40,000 ng/mL and 440 mg/dL - n.v. 20-120 ng/mL and <150 mg/dL respectively). Baseline lymphocytes CD4+ T-cell count was 19 cell/muL and HIV-RNA was 1,787,000 cp/mL. In addition, the patient resulted positive for EBV-DNA (1,297 cp/mL), CMV-DNA (266 cp/mL), and HBV-DNA (> 700,000,000 UI/mL), and for blood stool test. Suspecting a lymphoproliferative disorder evolving in haemophagocytic syndrome, a bone marrow biopsy was performed and steroid treatment was started. Consequently, we performed biopsies of the gut, lateral-cervical lymph node, and tonsil. Microscopical evaluation of hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) sections of the bone marrow showed a prominent lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with budding yeast cells inside macrophages, suggestive of histoplasmosis, which was confirmed by Grocott Methenamine Silver stain (GMS) and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) stain. Antifungal treatment with liposomal Amphotericin B was started while steroid therapy was gradually reduced. She rapidly became afebrile and, in the following weeks, we observed a slow regression of symptoms. Histological examination of submandibular lymph node, tonsil and colic mucosa also confirmed the diagnosis (Figures 1, 2 and 3). Histoplasma spp serology was negative, while culture of bone marrow aspirate showed H. capsulatum growth. After three weeks of induction therapy, she continued on maintenance therapy with itraconazole, and cART with tenofovir/emtricitabine + dolutegravir was prescribed. The patient was referred to the Outpatient Clinic. She attended at the first follow-up visit ten days after the hospital discharge with improved clinical conditions and blood exams. However in April 2016 she returned to Ivory Coast and was re-linked to care in October 2016. At the time of the visit lymphocytes CD4+ T count was 29 cell/muL, HIV-RNA was 153,300 cp/mL and HBV DNA was 212,600,000 UI/mL. During her stay in Ivory Coast, she interrupted both antiretroviral therapy and histoplasmosis maintenance therapy; moreover, at the moment of the new visit she was pregnant and after proper counseling, she decided to carry on the pregnancy. Only antiretroviral therapy with tenofovir/emtricitabine + atazanavir/ritonavir was re-started and a close follow-up was scheduled. After three weeks she was admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) for internal abortion, complicated by septic shock. She was treated with wide spectrum antibiotic therapy (meropenem and vancomycin) without any microbiological isolation and she went through several transfusions and mechanical ventilation. Once stabilized, she was transferred to our Department, she was febrile, pancytopenic and with a skin lesions on her chest, suggestive of histoplasmosis reactivation so that antifungal treatment with liposomal Amphotericin B was reintroduced. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed the suspect. The same day antiretroviral therapy with tenofovir/emtricitabine + dolutegravir was reintroduced. In the following weeks, a slow progressive improvement of the conditions was observed, therefore she was transferred to a facility with proper social support and health assistance. At the time of the last visit in December 2017, the patient was asymptomatic and fully adherent with cART and histoplasmosis prophylaxis. Last CD4+ T-cell count was 150 cell/muL and a low-level viral load was detected for HIV and HBV (33 copies/mL and 95 UI/mL respectively).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 19-year-old woman from Ivory Coast presented with persistent fever, chills, and profound asthenia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In February 2016, the patient was admitted to a peripheral hospital for persistent fever, tested positive on an HIV antibody screen, and was transferred to the Infectious and Tropical Diseases Department with high fever, chills, and deep asthenia.
subjective.past_medical_history: Newly diagnosed HIV-1 infection and chronic hepatitis B virus coinfection; originally from Ivory Coast.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent fever, chills, and profound asthenia.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: temperature max 38.8 C, HR 110 bpm. HEENT/Lymphatics: unilateral tonsillar hypertrophy and submandibular lymphadenopathy. On later readmission post-stay in Ivory Coast, she had fever and chest skin lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs: pancytopenia with Hb 8.7 g/dL (normal 12.0-16.0), WBC 3,050/uL (normal 4.00-10.80 x 10^3), platelets 80,000/uL (normal 130-400 x 10^3); LDH 5,201 U/L (normal 136-234), CRP 63.3 mg/L (normal <5.0), ferritin >40,000 ng/mL (normal 20-120), triglycerides 440 mg/dL (normal <150), positive fecal occult blood test, and negative Histoplasma serology.
objective.advanced_workup: Immunology/virology: baseline CD4+ T-cell count 19 cells/uL, HIV-RNA 1,787,000 copies/mL, EBV-DNA 1,297 copies/mL, CMV-DNA 266 copies/mL, and HBV-DNA >700,000,000 IU/mL. Biopsies of bone marrow, submandibular lymph node, tonsil, and colonic mucosa: prominent lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with intracellular budding yeast cells inside macrophages on H&E, GMS, and PAS stains.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis with secondary hemophagocytic syndrome in newly diagnosed advanced HIV-1 and HBV coinfection, complicated by relapse after treatment interruption in Ivory Coast. Confirmation: Bone marrow, submandibular lymph node, tonsil, and colonic mucosal biopsies (H&E, GMS, PAS) showing intrahistiocytic budding yeasts, and bone marrow aspirate culture growing Histoplasma capsulatum (repeat bone marrow biopsy also confirmed relapse). Plan & clinical course: Treated with 3 weeks of IV liposomal amphotericin B plus tapering steroids, followed by oral itraconazole maintenance and cART (tenofovir/emtricitabine + dolutegravir). After interrupting therapy in Ivory Coast and suffering a septic abortion, histoplasmosis reactivation was successfully re-treated with liposomal amphotericin B, itraconazole prophylaxis, and tenofovir/emtricitabine + dolutegravir; by December 2017, she was asymptomatic with CD4 150 cells/uL, HIV-RNA 33 copies/mL, and HBV-DNA 95 IU/mL.
